summary: Steel tower, 30 m (98 ft), present structure built 2012 per Alberta Wildfire's layer; a lookout ladder project is recorded for 1949. No source describes public visits.

access.note: Active Alberta Wildfire site; the layer lists access mode as drive. No source found says the public may visit.

events.note: Lookout ladder project completed, per the Canada Lookouts index citing the Department of Lands and Forests annual report for the year ended 31 March 1950
Present steel tower; year of construction per the Alberta Wildfire lookout layer

evidence.supports: steel tower, 30 m tall, elevation 730 m, present structure built 2012
each site staffed by a lookout observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: 1949 ladder project completed; cites the Department of Lands and Forests annual report for the year ended 31 March 1950
evidence.quote: 1949: The Hawk Hills lookout ladder project was completed. (Annual Report of the Department of Lands and Forests, FY ended 3/31/1950)

evidence.supports: listed under the Peace River Division
many Alberta lookouts rebuilt on the location of the first generation
evidence.quote: Many of Alberta’s 127 operational fire lookouts are rebuilt on the location of the first generation of lookouts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The layer's 2012 date is for the present structure. The 1949 ladder project is an older entry for the same site, so the two dates do not contradict each other.

sources.title: Alberta Wildfire: Wildfire Lookouts of Alberta (WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT) layer query
sources.publisher: Government of Alberta, FireSmart vector data service

notes_for_editor: The 1949 ladder-project entry comes from a Canada Lookouts web index that cites an annual report; the annual report itself was not read, so the entry is one step removed. The index puts the lookout under the Peace River Division. Present structure (2012) and the 1949 ladder project are both recorded; no source says whether the 2012 tower stands on the 1949 site. Not used: a Wikipedia article on a Hawk Hills in Red Deer County, which is a different place. The Alberta Wildfire observer blog posts from 2017 describe a Peace Country tower but do not name it, so they are not attributed here. No photos.
